Curate one reconciled nrDNA feature model against a clade ruleset (pure)

Source: R/curate_rrna.R
curate_rrna_core.Rd

Curate one reconciled nrDNA feature model against a clade ruleset (pure)

Usage

curate_rrna_core(
  features,
  params = rrna_params(),
  ref_pid = NULL,
  ref_cov = NULL,
  sample_lineage = NA,
  hit_lineage = NA,
  hit_is_nuclear_rrna = NA,
  sample_taxids = NA_character_,
  hit_taxids = NA_character_
)

Arguments

features

data.frame(element, type, start, stop, length, strand, ...) as produced by reconcile_features() / stored in the annotations table.

params

A ruleset from rrna_params().

ref_pid

Optional named numeric vector (element -> percent identity to the top reference), from the blast_ref_alignment table. Missing elements are skipped (identity check is opportunistic).

ref_cov

Optional named numeric vector (element -> fraction of the element covered by the reference alignment, blast_ref_alignment.aln_cov). The identity check is skipped when coverage is below min_ref_coverage, so a partial reference cannot raise a false low_identity flag.

sample_lineage, hit_lineage

Optional lineage strings for the contaminant check: the sample's assigned lineage vs. the lineage of the BLAST screen's unfiltered top hit (blast_screen.lineage), not the nuclear-rDNA reference candidates. An unknown lineage on either side raises contaminant_unchecked rather than passing silently.

hit_is_nuclear_rrna

Optional 0/1 (blast_screen.is_nuclear_rrna): whether that top hit is a nuclear rDNA record at all. 0 raises not_nuclear_rdna.

sample_taxids, hit_taxids

Optional rank-aligned taxid strings matching those lineages (samples.lineage_taxids, blast_screen.lineage_taxids). The comparison prefers them and falls back to the names when absent.

Value

list(features, flags, n_flags, notes) where features gains status ("ok"/"flag"), flags (comma-separated per-feature codes), and partial_start/partial_stop (1 on the free 5'/3' ends of a truncated feature, in its own orientation; NA elsewhere), and the sample-level flags/notes summarize missing anchors, ordering, etc.
